Directions: Read the following passage carefully, then answer each question that follows.
Context: The following is an excerpt from a novel set on the Caribbean island of Trinidad.
Content: It must have been about in `text(Third)` Standard that
Helen came into existence. For by then I used to look
forward to the library van on `text(Saturdays)` with the
greatest of impatience, having usually read the
`text(two)` books by `text(Monday)` morning.
Books transported you always into the familiar
solidity of chimneys and apple trees, the enviable
normality of real Girls and Boys who went a-
sleighing and built snowmen, ate potatoes, not rice,
went about in socks and shoes from morning until
night and called things by their proper names, never
saying 'washicong' for plimsoll* or 'crapaud' when
they meant a frog. Books transported you always into
Reality and Rightness, which were to be found
Abroad.
Thus it was that I fashioned Helen, my `text(double)`.
She was my age and height. She spent the summer
holidays at the sea-side with her aunt and uncle who
had a delightful orchard with apple trees and pear
trees in which sang chaffinches and blue tits, and
where `text(one)` could wander on terms of the closest
familiarity with cowslips and honeysuckle. Helen
loved to visit her Granny for then they sat by the
fireside and had tea with delicious scones and home-
made strawberry jam... Helen entered and ousted
all the other characters in the unending serial that I
had been spinning for Toddan and Doolarie from time
immemorial.
At `text(one)` time I took to putting on shoes the
moment I woke up on mornings and not removing
them again until bedtime. This caused some hilarity
in the household - 'What happen, Ma-Davis, yu
really takin'-in with ol'-age, eh?' enquired Mikey
solicitously. But when `text(one day)` I started to put on
socks to go to the shop, Tantie was not amused.
'Look, Madam, when yu start to wash yu own
clothes then yu could start to play the monkey-you
ever put-on socks to go down in the shop? What it is
take yu at-all?'
I loved rainy mornings, for then I could pretend it
was winter as I left for school bundled up in an old
jacket.
Helen wasn't even my `text(double)`. No, she couldn't be
called my `text(double)`. She was the Proper Me. And me, I
was her shadow hovering about in incompleteness.
For `text(doubleness)`, or this particular kind of
`text(doubleness)`, was a thing to be taken for granted. Why,
the whole of life was like a piece of cloth, with a
rightside and a wrongside. Just as there was a way
you spoke and a way you wrote, so there was the
`text(daily)` existence which you led, which of course
amounted only to marking time and makeshift, for
there was the Proper `text(daily)` round, not necessarily more
agreeable, simply the valid `text(one)`, the course of which
encompassed things like warming yourself before a
fire and having tea at `text(four o'clock)`; there were the
human types who were your neighbours and
guardians and playmates - but you were all marginal
together, for there were the beings whose validity
loomed at you out of every book, every picture.
